Why facilities are switching to autonomous cleaning.

Labour costs keep rising, and cleaning is the first budget that gets cut.

At 5,000 m² (about 53,820 ft²) an R5 gives back about three hours a day, which is 106 eight-hour shifts a year, running unsupervised every night.

Cleaning gets done, but there is no record to show for it.

Every run is logged automatically: area, time, route and completion, in a format that audit and procurement teams can verify.

Cleaning costs move every year, and budgets are set in advance.

Robots move part of the cost base from hours to equipment, which is planned once instead of renegotiated. That holds whether you run the site yourself or clean it under contract.

Where LionsBot robots already work.

Aviation

Southeast Asia

International airport: overnight cleaning across all departure terminals.

Night shifts were expensive and hard to staff. The operator needed 15,000 m² (about 161,000 ft²) covered without supervision, and a record of every run to hand to the airport authority.

R5 units now cover the terminals overnight, unsupervised, and every run writes its own log. At 15,000 m² that is roughly 10 hours of scrubbing a night nobody has to staff.

Healthcare

United Kingdom & Europe

Regional hospital group: audit-grade hygiene records across three sites.

Paper records were a problem when inspectors came. The purchasing team wanted a digital record of every shift, and the same overnight standard on all three sites, without hiring anyone.

The same route now runs on every site, and each shift produces its own record.

Logistics

Australia & APAC

40,000 m² distribution centre: 7-day continuous floor cleaning.

Cleaners and forklifts were working the same aisles on every shift. The site needed floor coverage that did not have to be booked in with a shift supervisor every night.

Robots now work the aisles on a seven-day cycle, around the forklifts. At 40,000 m² (about 431,000 ft²) that is roughly 26 hours of scrubbing a day.

Retail & Malls

Singapore

Major shopping mall: continuous cleaning across 80,000 m² of public concourse.

At the busiest times of day, cleaning a concourse meant wet floors and complaints. The property needed machines quiet and predictable enough to keep working through trading hours.

R5 units now clean the concourse while the mall is open. At 80,000 m² (about 861,000 ft²) that is roughly 52 hours of scrubbing a day across the fleet.

Education

Japan & APAC

University campus: library and common area cleaning without disrupting students.

Cleaning the library in opening hours meant noise complaints, and during exams it was not an option at all. The campus needed a machine quiet enough to run beside people studying.

An R3 Vac now runs the library through opening hours, taking under ten minutes of cleaner attention a day.

Facility Services

Germany & EMEA

National facilities management contractor: deploying LionsBot R5 robots across 40 client sites to protect fixed-price contract margins.

Wage rises were shrinking the margin on contracts already signed at a fixed price. The contractor had to take labour out of scrubbing without going back to clients to renegotiate.

R5 units now do the scrubbing, and the contracts were never reopened.

Common questions.

What is LionsBot?

LionsBot International is a Singapore-based company that designs and engineers autonomous commercial cleaning robots. They are deployed in airports, hospitals, shopping malls and logistics centres across 40+ countries.

Where is LionsBot based?

LionsBot is headquartered in Singapore at Punggol Digital District. Engineering, testing and quality standards for the whole range sit with one team there, so every robot is designed and engineered to the same standard.

What autonomous cleaning robots does LionsBot make?

LionsBot makes autonomous cleaning robots for commercial floors, covering both scrubbing and vacuuming. The range runs from compact machines for tight indoor spaces to larger scrubbers for big open floors. The R5 is the flagship, at 5,000 m² per charge.

Which industries use LionsBot robots?

LionsBot robots are deployed in hospitality (airports and hotels), healthcare (hospitals and medical centres), retail (shopping malls), logistics (warehouses and distribution centres), education (universities and schools), and facility management contracts.

Which countries does LionsBot operate in?

LionsBot's dealer network spans 40+ countries across Asia Pacific, the Middle East, Europe and the Americas, including India, the UAE, the United Kingdom, Australia and the United States, providing local sales, deployment and after-sales support for the full autonomous cleaning robot range.

What is the difference between an autonomous cleaning robot and a traditional cleaning contract?

An autonomous cleaning robot like the LionsBot R5 scrubs floors on a fixed schedule without a human operator, producing a digital log of every run. A traditional cleaning contract is staffed on a roster, with completed work recorded by hand.

How do I get a LionsBot robot for my site?

Enquire through lionsbot.com. LionsBot robots are available in 40+ countries, with local deployment and after-sales support.

How much does a LionsBot robot cost?

Three things drive it: how much floor you need covered, what type of floor it is, and how the robot is configured. We can work that out with you for your own site.
